Carbamazepine and gabapentin can worsen absence seizures by aggravating thalamocortical spike and wave activity, which is why drug choice matters here.

items.stem: A 74-year-old woman taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation is brought in with sudden right hemiparesis and vomiting. Computed tomography shows a left basal ganglia hemorrhage, and her international normalized ratio is 3.8. Which reversal strategy is best?
options: Fresh frozen plasma as the only reversal agent
Oral vitamin K alone with repeat INR testing
Platelet transfusion to correct bleeding time
Prothrombin complex plus vitamin K
items.explanation: Warfarin-associated intracerebral hemorrhage needs rapid correction of coagulopathy, and prothrombin complex concentrate normalizes the international normalized ratio faster than plasma with less volume load, while intravenous vitamin K sustains the effect after the factors wear off. Plasma alone is slow and bulky. Oral vitamin K is too slow, and platelets are not indicated because the defect is in clotting factors.

items.stem: A 22-year-old man has dysarthria, a wing-beating tremor, and a Kayser-Fleischer ring. Serum ceruloplasmin is low. Which defect underlies his disease?
options: Mutation of the ceruloplasmin gene
Mutation of the ATP7A copper transporter
ATP7B copper ATPase mutation
Mutation of the HFE iron regulatory gene
items.explanation: Wilson disease is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in ATP7B, which impair biliary copper excretion and incorporation of copper into ceruloplasmin, leading to hepatic and basal ganglia copper accumulation. Aceruloplasminemia from a ceruloplasmin gene mutation causes brain iron overload, ATP7A mutations cause Menkes disease in boys, and HFE variants cause hereditary hemochromatosis, which does not produce this copper syndrome.

items.stem: A 27-year-old woman has painful loss of vision in her left eye over 4 days, along with a relative afferent pupillary defect and a normal optic disc. Which statement about intravenous methylprednisolone is correct?
options: It speeds recovery without changing final acuity
It prevents conversion to multiple sclerosis for 10 years
It improves final acuity more than oral prednisone alone
It is contraindicated because it raises relapse risk
items.explanation: Acute optic neuritis recovers spontaneously in most patients, and high-dose intravenous corticosteroids hasten recovery without altering the long-term acuity outcome. The optic neuritis treatment trial found that standard-dose oral prednisone alone gave no benefit and was linked to more recurrences. Steroids do not alter the long-term risk of multiple sclerosis, and they are not contraindicated.

items.stem: A 66-year-old retired teacher reports that over 18 months she has trouble finding common words and has begun to substitute 'the thing for cutting' for 'knife.' Comprehension of single words is now impaired, and she no longer recognizes what a pepper grinder is for. Episodic memory and navigation are preserved. Which pattern of atrophy is expected on imaging?
options: Bilateral hippocampal and medial temporal atrophy
Asymmetric left anterior temporal atrophy
Left posterior perisylvian and inferior parietal atrophy
Bilateral frontal pole and anterior cingulate atrophy
items.explanation: Fluent speech with loss of word meaning and object knowledge is semantic variant primary progressive aphasia, caused by left-predominant anterior temporal degeneration. Hippocampal atrophy matches typical Alzheimer amnestic disease. Posterior perisylvian atrophy fits the logopenic variant, which impairs repetition and phonologic loops rather than semantics. Frontal pole atrophy accompanies behavioral variant frontotemporal dementia, with disinhibition and apathy instead of progressive loss of meaning.

items.stem: A 71-year-old man has 5 years of progressive weakness of finger flexion and knee extension, with difficulty swallowing solid food. Creatine kinase is mildly elevated. He has had no response to a 3-month trial of high-dose prednisone. Muscle biopsy is most likely to show which finding?
options: Perifascicular atrophy with perimysial vessel inflammation
Fiber type grouping with angulated atrophic fibers
Ragged red fibers with cytochrome oxidase negative fibers
Rimmed vacuoles with endomysial inflammatory infiltrates
items.explanation: Selective finger flexor and quadriceps weakness with dysphagia and steroid resistance in an older adult is typical of inclusion body myositis, whose biopsy shows rimmed vacuoles and endomysial T cell invasion of fibers. Perifascicular atrophy suggests dermatomyositis. Fiber type grouping reflects chronic denervation and reinnervation. Ragged red fibers point to a mitochondrial myopathy. Biopsy therefore separates these four muscle diseases.

items.stem: A 33-year-old woman with focal impaired awareness seizures preceded by a rising epigastric sensation has had two adequate trials of well-tolerated antiseizure medications without seizure freedom. Magnetic resonance imaging shows left hippocampal sclerosis concordant with her seizures. What is the best next step?
options: Trial of a third antiseizure medication as monotherapy
Referral to an epilepsy surgery center for evaluation
Placement of a vagus nerve stimulator
Initiation of the ketogenic diet
items.explanation: Failure of two appropriately chosen and tolerated medications defines drug-resistant epilepsy, and the chance of seizure freedom with a third drug is small. Concordant mesial temporal sclerosis makes her an excellent surgical candidate, with seizure freedom in a majority after temporal lobectomy. Neurostimulation and dietary therapy are reserved for patients who are not resection candidates.

items.stem: A 58-year-old man had a transient episode of right monocular visual loss. Duplex imaging shows 75 percent stenosis of the ipsilateral internal carotid artery. He is neurologically normal now. By what time frame should carotid endarterectomy ideally be performed?
options: After 3 months of medical stabilization
Only if a second event occurs
Within 2 weeks of the event
Within 24 hours as an emergency
items.explanation: Symptomatic carotid stenosis of 70 percent or more carries its highest recurrent stroke risk in the first days to weeks, and the benefit of endarterectomy is greatest when performed within 2 weeks. Waiting months forfeits that benefit. Waiting for another event exposes the patient to disabling stroke. Emergency surgery within a day is not required and carries higher perioperative risk.

items.stem: A 68-year-old woman with asthma has a bilateral postural hand tremor that makes holding a cup difficult from a cup. Her father had a similar tremor. Which medication is the most appropriate first choice for her?
options: Primidone
Propranolol
Levodopa
Trihexyphenidyl
items.explanation: Essential tremor is treated first with propranolol or primidone, and primidone is the better choice here because nonselective beta blockers can provoke bronchospasm in asthma. Levodopa treats Parkinson disease and does not improve essential tremor. Trihexyphenidyl has limited effect on action tremor and its anticholinergic effects are poorly tolerated in older adults, who may become confused.

items.stem: A 49-year-old man has 3 years of progressive spastic paraparesis and gait decline without relapses. Magnetic resonance imaging shows spinal cord atrophy and a few periventricular lesions, and cerebrospinal fluid shows oligoclonal bands. Which disease-modifying therapy is approved for his condition?
options: Interferon beta-1a
Glatiramer acetate
Natalizumab
Ocrelizumab
items.explanation: Gradual progression from onset with supportive imaging and oligoclonal bands defines primary progressive multiple sclerosis, and the anti-CD20 antibody ocrelizumab is the first agent shown to slow disability progression in this form. Interferon beta and glatiramer acetate lack proven benefit for primary progressive disease. Natalizumab failed to show benefit in progressive trials and carries a risk of leukoencephalopathy.

items.stem: A 38-year-old woman has a 3-year history of difficulty climbing stairs and now wakes with morning headaches and daytime sleepiness. Examination shows symmetric proximal weakness with mildly elevated creatine kinase, and forced vital capacity falls 25 percent when she lies flat. Which enzyme deficiency is most likely?
options: Myophosphorylase
Carnitine palmitoyltransferase II
Acid alpha-glucosidase
Debranching enzyme
items.explanation: Proximal limb weakness with early diaphragm involvement and a large drop in vital capacity when supine suggests late-onset Pompe disease, a lysosomal glycogen storage disorder due to acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency, treatable with enzyme replacement. Myophosphorylase deficiency (McArdle) causes exercise cramps and myoglobinuria. Carnitine palmitoyltransferase II deficiency causes prolonged exercise-induced rhabdomyolysis rather than fixed proximal weakness.

items.stem: A 19-year-old woman is brought in after an event of 4 minutes of thrashing with pelvic thrusting while her eyes remained tightly closed, followed by immediate clear speech. Which finding most strongly favors a functional seizure?
options: Lateral tongue laceration
Postictal confusion for 20 minutes
Cyanosis during the tonic phase
Eyes closed throughout the event
items.explanation: Persistent forced eye closure during a convulsive event is one of the more reliable signs of functional seizures, as are long duration, asynchronous movements, and rapid recovery. A lateral tongue bite, postictal confusion, and cyanosis all favor an epileptic generalized tonic-clonic seizure, though no single sign is perfect and video electroencephalography remains the reference standard.

items.stem: A 36-year-old woman 10 days postpartum has recurrent thunderclap headaches. Computed tomography is normal, and angiography shows multifocal segmental narrowing and dilation of intracranial arteries that normalizes on repeat imaging at 12 weeks. Which treatment is most appropriate?
options: High-dose intravenous methylprednisolone
Intravenous alteplase
A calcium channel blocker such as nimodipine
Sumatriptan for each headache
items.explanation: Recurrent thunderclap headache with reversible multifocal vasoconstriction is reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome, often postpartum or triggered by vasoactive drugs. Calcium channel blockers are commonly used to ease headaches and vasospasm. Corticosteroids are associated with worse outcomes. Alteplase has no role without thrombosis, and triptans are vasoconstrictors that can precipitate the syndrome or worsen it, so they are avoided.

items.stem: A 77-year-old man with Parkinson disease develops well-formed visual hallucinations of children in the house, without delirium. A medication review shows no recent additions. After stopping an anticholinergic, which antipsychotic is most appropriate if treatment is needed?
options: Haloperidol at bedtime
Low-dose quetiapine
Risperidone at low dose
Olanzapine at low dose
items.explanation: Parkinson disease psychosis is treated by removing offending drugs and, when needed, using an antipsychotic with minimal dopamine blockade, such as quetiapine, clozapine, or pimavanserin. Haloperidol, risperidone, and olanzapine block D2 receptors enough to worsen motor function substantially. Because dementia raises mortality with antipsychotics, the lowest effective dose is used, and the response is reviewed often.

items.stem: A 29-year-old man hospitalized with Guillain-Barre syndrome on day 5 has ascending weakness, areflexia, and difficulty counting to 20 in one breath. Which bedside measurement most strongly supports transfer to the intensive care unit for elective intubation?
options: Forced vital capacity below 20 mL/kg
Oxygen saturation of 94 percent on room air
Respiratory rate of 18 breaths per minute
Arterial pH of 7.38
items.explanation: Serial forced vital capacity is the best predictor of respiratory failure in Guillain-Barre syndrome, and a value under 20 mL/kg, or a fall of 30 percent from baseline, warrants intubation planning, along with maximal inspiratory pressure weaker than minus 30 cm of water. Oxygen saturation, respiratory rate, and arterial pH stay normal until late and give false reassurance.
